VRAM prices plummeted. It was $6...$10/GB for last gen and now is $2...$5/GB (allegedly; from sources in the industry).
+ MCDs are also N6 (same production line and process as 7nm) so I suppose it's about the same price:
-RX6700XT has a 335 sq mm die on 7nm.
-RX7800XT (and 7700XT) has a 200 sq mm die(CCD) on 5nm and ~146 sq mm die(4x 36.6 sq mm MCDs) on the N6 die (same as 7nm process). Total 346 sq mm.

16GB now are $30...$40 cheaper than 12GB then. I can't imagine the die difference being more than that so they'd at least balance out, if not be cheaper now.

Just like Nvidia (where 4070 is a 3060 on N4 instead vs Samsung 8nm and some extra $30 for better power delivery and cooling - but $50...$60 cheaper VRAM-, but jumps from a $330 to a $600 MSRP) AMD also tries to milk us...and people praise it because it's not as bad...

If anything, 7800XT should be a 7700XTX (named appropriately for that die size, if we consider removing non XT naming altogether, because it's confusing vs Ryzen non X) and cost <$450. 7700XT (as is) belongs at ~$370. Just because RTX 4000 is garbage for the money, doesn't make RX 7000 good...just not as bad. Given that 7600 is available at ~$230, I hope soon would be the case for 7800XT and 7700XT to drop in a few months.
